A school district in Texas is going all-in on iPads and MacBook Neo in a deal worth $11 million. The Beaumont Independent School District has decided to ditch its fleet of Chromebooks in favor of Apple products, citing greater reliability, lower costs, and better performance.

According to the *Beaumont Enterprise* this week, the Beaumont Independent School District Board of Trustees has approved a four-year, $11.19 million lease plan to upgrade its technology.

Under the deal, the district will provide 14,585 Apple devices to students and staff from pre-K through 12th grade. The new Apple products will replace a fleet of aging Chromebooks, many of which are five years old. The district spends nearly $500,000 a year to repair and support its Chromebook fleet.

The new plan includes more than 4,000 iPads for pre-K through 2nd grade students, and 9,500 MacBook Neo devices for students in grades 3 through 12. The district has also set aside 1,000 MacBook Neo units for teachers.

The district compared the MacBook Neo against offerings from Lenovo and Asus, ultimately concluding that the MacBook Neo was "the strongest performing and most reliable device evaluated." Apple's more favorable financing terms and the availability of AppleCare were also deciding factors.

Read the full report at the *Beaumont Enterprise*.
